name: Yang Liwei
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; joined PLA Air Force at 18 and became a fighter pilot by 22, but was not selected for astronaut training until age 33 (1998) and flew Shenzhou 5 at age 38 (2003).
early_history_summary: Yang joined the PLA in 1983 at age 18 and entered the Air Force Second Flight Academy, graduating in 1987 as a fighter pilot. He accumulated 1,350 flight hours but had no notable public achievement before astronaut selection in 1998.
family_context_summary: Born to a teacher mother and an accountant father at a state agricultural firm in Suizhong County, Liaoning; described as a hardworking, modest family.

name: Diane von Fürstenberg
milestone_by_age_26: Sold her first dress collection during New York Fashion Week in 1970 at age 23 and established her namesake fashion label by 1972 at age 25.
early_history_summary: Born in Brussels to Jewish parents, Diane Halfin studied economics at the University of Geneva, where she met Prince Egon von Fürstenberg. After marrying in 1969, she apprenticed with textile manufacturer Angelo Ferretti in Italy, learning about cut, color, and fabric. She brought her first jersey dress collection to New York in 1970 and presented it to Vogue editor Diana Vreeland, launching her commercial career.
family_context_summary: Born to Jewish parents in Brussels; mother Liliane Nahmias was a Greek-born Holocaust survivor who survived Auschwitz and Ravensbrück, weighing 49 pounds at liberation. Father Leon Halfin was a Bessarabian-born businessman who sought refuge in Switzerland during the war.
parent_family_domain_summary: No direct fashion or design background in the family; however, marrying into the German princely House of Fürstenberg provided aristocratic connections and social access that opened doors in the fashion world.
primary_early_advantage_tags: aristocratic marriage, social access, Vreeland endorsement, textile apprenticeship, Holocaust survivor mother
evidence_summary: Diane von Fürstenberg was born in Brussels in 1946 to a Holocaust-survivor mother and a businessman father. She married Prince Egon von Fürstenberg in 1969 at age 22, gaining aristocratic social access that opened doors in New York fashion. She apprenticed with textile manufacturer Angelo Ferretti in Italy, then launched her first jersey dress collection in New York in 1970, presented to Vogue editor Diana Vreeland. By 1972, she had established her namesake label, well before the iconic wrap dress of 1974. Her mother's survival ethic ('fear is not an option') and the social capital from her marriage were key early advantages.
starting_point: Born in Brussels in 1946 to a Jewish family; mother was a Holocaust survivor from Auschwitz, father a Bessarabian-born businessman who fled to Switzerland during WWII. Middle-class-to-comfortable background.
current_position: Fashion designer and philanthropist; founder of DVF brand; net worth estimated ~$1.2 billion; resides in New York City.

trajectory.event: Sold her first jersey dress collection during New York Fashion Week after presenting prototypes to Vogue editor Diana Vreeland.
Established her namesake fashion label, Diane von Fürstenberg, in New York.
Debuted the iconic wrap dress, which became a massive commercial hit and defined 1970s American fashion.
Featured on the cover of Newsweek; by this time selling over one million wrap dresses.
Re-launched the DVF brand successfully and became president of the Council of Fashion Designers of America (CFDA).
Named to Time magazine's list of the 100 most influential people in the world.

name: Yasmeen Lari
milestone_by_age_26: Graduated from the Oxford School of Architecture in 1964 at age 23, returned to Pakistan, and founded Lari Associates in Karachi, becoming Pakistan's first female architect.
early_history_summary: Born in Dera Ghazi Khan in 1941, Lari grew up in Lahore in a prominent Iraqi Biradari clan. Her father, Zafarul Ahsan, was an ICS officer who chaired the Lahore Improvement Trust and exposed Lari to architecture and urban development. At age 15, she moved to London with her family, studied arts for two years after initial rejection from architecture school, then was accepted into the Oxford School of Architecture, graduating in 1964.
family_context_summary: Born into a privileged, well-connected family; father Zafarul Ahsan was a senior ICS officer who became deputy commissioner of Lahore and chairman of the Lahore Improvement Trust, working on major development projects. Mother Nabiun Nisa was educated and active in refugee welfare.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a senior civil servant directly responsible for urban development and housing projects in Lahore, which exposed Lari to architecture and city planning from a young age and motivated her to pursue the field.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father ICS officer, urban development exposure, Oxford architecture, privileged family, Pakistan first female architect
evidence_summary: Yasmeen Lari was born in 1941 into a privileged Pakistani family; her father was a senior civil servant who chaired the Lahore Improvement Trust and exposed her to architecture and urban planning. She moved to London at 15, eventually studying architecture at Oxford, graduating in 1964. She returned to Pakistan and founded Lari Associates, becoming the country's first female architect at age 23. Her father's position and encouragement, plus her Oxford education, were key early advantages. She faced gender-based challenges on construction sites but overcame them with her privileged background and married status.
starting_point: Born in 1941 in Dera Ghazi Khan, Pakistan into a privileged family; father was a senior Indian Civil Service officer who became deputy commissioner of Lahore and chaired development authorities.
current_position: Retired from architectural practice since 2000; runs Heritage Foundation Pakistan focused on humanitarian relief and zero-carbon housing; awarded RIBA Royal Gold Medal in 2023; resides in Karachi, Pakistan.

trajectory.event: Graduated from the Oxford School of Architecture and founded Lari Associates in Karachi, becoming Pakistan's first female architect.
Designed the Angoori Bagh Housing project in Lahore, Pakistan's first public housing plan.
Co-founded the Heritage Foundation of Pakistan with her husband Suhail Zaheer Lari and became first president of the Institute of Architects Pakistan.
Completed the Finance and Trade Centre in Karachi, one of her most iconic commercial buildings.
Retired from architectural practice to focus on heritage conservation and humanitarian work.
Awarded the Jane Drew Prize for her contributions to architecture.
Awarded the RIBA Royal Gold Medal, becoming the first Pakistani recipient.

name: Soumya Swaminathan
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; was completing medical education (MBBS from Armed Forces Medical College, then MD from AIIMS Delhi) and had not yet begun her notable TB research career, which started at NIRT in 1992 at age 33.

She studied medicine at Armed Forces Medical College Pune and AIIMS Delhi, but her impactful research career began only after joining the National Institute for Research in Tuberculosis in 1992.
family_context_summary: Daughter of M.S. Swaminathan, the renowned geneticist regarded as the father of India's Green Revolution; grew up surrounded by scientific research, laboratories, and field experiments.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was one of India's most prominent agricultural scientists, providing deep immersion in a scientific research environment from childhood.
evidence_summary: Soumya Swaminathan was born in 1959 to M.S. Swaminathan, India's most famous agricultural scientist. She studied medicine at AFMC Pune and AIIMS Delhi, but her notable research career in tuberculosis began only in 1992 at age 33 when she joined NIRT Chennai. She later became WHO's first Chief Scientist, but no material milestone occurred by age 26.

name: Halston
milestone_by_age_26: Opened his own hat shop on Michigan Avenue in Chicago in 1953 at age 21, building a celebrity clientele including Kim Novak, Gloria Swanson, and Fran Allison, and by 1958 became head milliner at Bergdorf Goodman in New York.
early_history_summary: Born Roy Halston Frowick in Des Moines, Iowa, he learned sewing from his grandmother and began making hats as a teenager. He studied at Indiana University and the School of the Art Institute of Chicago, where he started selling hats out of a beauty salon at the Ambassador Hotel. By 1953, he had his own hat shop on Michigan Avenue, and by 1958 he moved to New York to work for milliner Lily Daché before becoming head milliner at Bergdorf Goodman.
family_context_summary: Born to a Norwegian-American accountant father and a stay-at-home mother in Des Moines, Iowa; modest middle-class upbringing. Learned sewing from his grandmother, who sparked his early interest in hat-making.
parent_family_domain_summary: No direct fashion industry background in the family; grandmother taught him sewing, which was a formative but informal influence rather than professional domain transfer.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Chicago Michigan Avenue boutique, Bergdorf Goodman, celebrity clientele, grandmother sewing, Art Institute of Chicago
evidence_summary: Halston was born in 1932 in Des Moines, Iowa, to a modest middle-class family. He learned sewing from his grandmother and began making hats as a teenager. After studying at the Art Institute of Chicago, he opened his own hat shop on Michigan Avenue in 1953 at age 21, quickly building a celebrity clientele. By 1958, he moved to New York and became head milliner at Bergdorf Goodman, one of the country's most prestigious retail outlets. His 1961 pillbox hat for Jackie Kennedy's inauguration catapulted him to national fame, but his material milestone—owning a successful hat business with celebrity clients—was achieved by age 21.
starting_point: Born in 1932 in Des Moines, Iowa to a Norwegian-American accountant father and stay-at-home mother; modest middle-class family. Learned sewing from his grandmother.
current_position: Died on March 26, 1990 at age 57 in San Francisco, California from AIDS-related cancer; final role: iconic American fashion designer and founder of Halston Limited.

trajectory.event: Opened his own hat shop on Michigan Avenue in Chicago, building a celebrity clientele including Kim Novak and Gloria Swanson.
Moved to New York and became head milliner at Bergdorf Goodman, the country's premier luxury retailer.
Designed the pillbox hat worn by Jacqueline Kennedy at JFK's presidential inauguration, catapulting him to national fame.
Expanded into women's ready-to-wear fashion, establishing Halston Ltd. and defining modern American glamour.
Became one of the defining designers of 1970s American fashion, dressing the Studio 54 jet-set including Liza Minnelli and Bianca Jagger.
Lost control of the Halston brand after a series of ill-advised business decisions and corporate transactions.
Died on March 26, 1990 in San Francisco from AIDS-related cancer.

name: Peter Sauber
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; began amateur racing in 1967 at age 24 but won the Swiss sports car championship only in 1970 at age 27, just past the cutoff.
early_history_summary: Trained as an electrician, Peter Sauber became a car salesman in Hinwil, Switzerland. He started amateur racing in 1967 at age 23 in a Volkswagen Beetle, then built the Sauber C1 sports car in his parents' basement, winning the 1970 Swiss hillclimb championship at age 27.
family_context_summary: Family owned a traffic light business in Zurich; Peter chose not to run the family business and instead pursued motorsport. Not documented as wealthy or connected to racing prior to his own entry.
parent_family_domain_summary: Family business was in traffic lights, not motorsport; no direct domain advantage transferred.
evidence_summary: Peter Sauber was born in 1943 in Zurich, Switzerland. His family owned a traffic light business, which he declined to run. He started amateur racing at 23 in 1967 and built the Sauber C1 in his parents' basement, but his first championship win came in 1970 at age 27, just past the age-26 cutoff. He later built Sauber into a Formula One team, but no material milestone occurred by age 26.

name: Hans Rosling
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; was still a medical student at Uppsala University (studied 1967–1974) and did not become a licensed physician until 1976 at age 28. His notable career began with fieldwork in Mozambique in 1979.
early_history_summary: Hans Rosling studied statistics and medicine at Uppsala University from 1967 to 1974, and public health at St. John's Medical College Bangalore in 1972. He became a licensed physician in 1976 and served as district medical officer in Mozambique from 1979 to 1981, where he discovered the disease konzo. His PhD came in 1986.
family_context_summary: Born in Uppsala, Sweden, the only child in a working-class family. Met his wife Agneta in grade school.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; working-class family with no apparent academic or medical background.
evidence_summary: Hans Rosling was born in 1948 in Uppsala, Sweden, to a working-class family. He studied medicine at Uppsala University from 1967 to 1974 but did not become a licensed physician until 1976 at age 28. His impactful career began with fieldwork in Mozambique in 1979 and his discovery of konzo. He later co-founded Gapminder and became famous for TED talks, but no material milestone occurred by age 26.

name: Faiza Al-Kharafi
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; was completing her BSc at Ain Shams University in Egypt and had not yet begun her graduate research or academic career. Her notable achievements came later with her PhD from Kuwait University and her presidency of Kuwait University (1993–2002).
early_history_summary: Faiza Al-Kharafi was born in Kuwait and earned a BSc from Ain Shams University in Egypt before returning to Kuwait to pursue MSc and PhD degrees from Kuwait University. Her research career in corrosion science and electrochemistry developed during and after her graduate studies, with no notable public milestone by age 26.
family_context_summary: Born in Kuwait; family background not extensively documented in reviewed sources, though she was able to study abroad in Egypt, suggesting a comfortable family situation.
evidence_summary: Faiza Al-Kharafi was born in 1946 in Kuwait. She earned a BSc from Ain Shams University in Egypt and later MSc and PhD from Kuwait University. She became a professor of chemistry, president of Kuwait University (1993–2002), and won the L'Oréal-UNESCO Award for Women in Science in 2011. However, no material milestone occurred by age 26, when she was still in early academic training.

name: Anja Pärson
milestone_by_age_26: Won gold in the giant slalom at the 1998 Junior World Championships at age 17, then won her first World Cup race (a slalom at Mammoth Mountain) in December 1998 at age 17, becoming the fifth Swedish woman to win a World Cup slalom.
early_history_summary: Born in Tärnaby, Sweden, a village of ~500 people that also produced skiing legend Ingemar Stenmark, Pärson was put on skis as soon as she could walk and began racing at age seven. Her father Anders, himself a former elite skier, coached her in her formative years. She made her World Cup debut at age 16 in March 1998 and won her first World Cup race at 17 in December 1998.
family_context_summary: Born in Tärnaby, Sweden, a tiny Arctic Circle village that produced skiing legends Ingemar Stenmark and Stig Strand. Father Anders Pärson was himself one of Sweden's best skiers and served as Anja's coach in her formative years. Mother Madeleine and older sister Frida were also involved in skiing.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Anders was a former elite skier who coached Anja from childhood, providing direct domain expertise and sustained individualized training. Growing up in Tärnaby, the same village as Ingemar Stenmark, immersed her in an elite skiing culture from birth.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father coach, Tärnaby skiing culture, Stenmark lineage, early racing age 7, Sámi roots, junior world champion
evidence_summary: Anja Pärson was born in 1981 in Tärnaby, Sweden, a tiny village that produced skiing legend Ingemar Stenmark. Her father Anders, a former elite skier, coached her from childhood, and she began racing at age seven. She made her World Cup debut at 16, won junior world championship gold at 17, and her first World Cup race at 17 in December 1998. The combination of her father's coaching, the Tärnaby skiing ecosystem, and her natural physical talent created an elite performance pipeline. She went on to win 42 World Cup races, 7 World Championship golds, and Olympic gold.
starting_point: Born in 1981 in Tärnaby, Sweden, a tiny Arctic Circle village (pop. ~500) that produced skiing legend Ingemar Stenmark; father Anders was a former elite skier who became her coach.
current_position: Retired from competitive skiing in March 2012; lives in Umeå, Sweden with wife Filippa and children; runs a company called 'She Likes' promoting products; estimated net worth not publicly documented.

trajectory.event: Won gold in the giant slalom at the Junior World Championships and her first World Cup slalom race at Mammoth Mountain, California.
Won slalom gold at the World Championships in St. Anton, becoming the youngest medalist at those championships.
Won her first overall Alpine Skiing World Cup title, cementing her status as the world's top female alpine skier.
Won Olympic gold in the slalom at the Turin Winter Olympics, plus silver and two bronze medals.
Won three gold medals at the World Championships in Åre, Sweden, becoming the first racer to hold world titles in all five Alpine disciplines.
Retired from competitive skiing on March 15, 2012, exactly 14 years after her first World Cup start.

name: Wojciech Kilar
milestone_by_age_26: Composed his first film score for the documentary 'Narciarze' (Skiers) in 1958 at age 26, launching a film music career that would span over 100 titles. Also won second prize for 'Little Overture' at the 5th Youth Festival in Warsaw in 1955 at age 23.
early_history_summary: Born in Lwów, Poland (now Lviv, Ukraine) in 1932 to a gynecologist father and theater actress mother, Kilar fled with his family to Rzeszów in 1944 to escape the Soviet army. He began piano studies there and won 2nd prize at a Young Talents' Competition in 1947 at age 15. He studied composition and piano at the State Higher School of Music in Katowice under Bolesław Woytowicz, graduating with distinction in 1955, then continued postgraduate studies in Kraków. He attended the Darmstadt International Summer Courses in 1957 and composed his first film score in 1958.
family_context_summary: Born in Lwów, Poland to a gynecologist father and a theater actress mother; professional, educated family that encouraged his musical education despite his initial reluctance to play piano.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a medical doctor (gynecologist) and mother was a theater actress; while neither was directly in music, the family was culturally sophisticated and encouraged artistic education, and the mother's theater background may have influenced his later affinity for film music.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Bolesław Woytowicz mentor, Katowice Music Academy, Darmstadt courses, Nadia Boulanger, Polish avant-garde, doctor father actress mother
evidence_summary: Wojciech Kilar was born in 1932 in Lwów, Poland to a doctor father and actress mother. After fleeing to Rzeszów in 1944, he began piano studies and won a competition at 15. He studied composition under Bolesław Woytowicz at the State Higher School of Music in Katowice, graduating with distinction in 1955, and won second prize for 'Little Overture' at the Youth Festival in Warsaw that same year. He attended the Darmstadt avant-garde courses in 1957 and composed his first film score in 1958 at age 26. His mentors—Woytowicz, and later Nadia Boulanger in Paris—were key accelerators. He co-founded the Polish avant-garde movement with Penderecki and Górecki.
starting_point: Born in 1932 in Lwów, Poland (now Lviv, Ukraine) to a gynecologist father and theater actress mother; professional, educated family displaced by WWII to Rzeszów in 1944.
current_position: Died on December 29, 2013 at age 81 in Katowice, Poland; final status: one of Poland's greatest composers, recipient of the Order of the White Eagle (2012).

trajectory.event: Graduated with distinction from the State Higher School of Music in Katowice and won second prize for 'Little Overture' at the 5th Youth Festival in Warsaw.
Composed his first film score for the documentary 'Narciarze' (Skiers), launching his film music career.
Received the Lili Boulanger Memorial Fund Award in Boston and studied composition under Nadia Boulanger in Paris on a French government scholarship.
Composed the symphonic poem 'Krzesany,' a harbinger of the New Romantic breakthrough in Polish music.
Composed the score for Francis Ford Coppola's 'Bram Stoker's Dracula,' winning the ASCAP Award and gaining international recognition.
Won the César Award for Best Film Music for 'The Pianist' and received a BAFTA nomination.
Received the Order of the White Eagle, Poland's highest distinction.
Died on December 29, 2013 in Katowice, Poland.

name: John Howe

family_context_summary: Born in Vancouver and raised on a farm in Keremeos, British Columbia; painfully shy as a child, he immersed himself in drawing and fantasy illustration. Family background not extensively documented.
evidence_summary: John Howe was born in 1957 in Vancouver, Canada, and grew up on a farm in British Columbia. name: Chris Benoit
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Stampede British Commonwealth Mid-Heavyweight Championship on March 18, 1988 at age 20, and went on to wrestle for New Japan Pro-Wrestling, winning the IWGP Junior Heavyweight Championship in 1990 at age 23.
early_history_summary: Born in Montreal and raised in Edmonton, Alberta, Benoit idolized the Dynamite Kid and Bret Hart from childhood, attending Stampede Wrestling events from age 12. He began training at age 17 in Stu Hart's famous 'Dungeon' and debuted for Stampede Wrestling in November 1985 at age 18. He won his first title—the Stampede British Commonwealth Mid-Heavyweight Championship—in March 1988 at age 20, then went to Japan to train with New Japan Pro-Wrestling.
family_context_summary: Born in Montreal to Michael and Margaret Benoit; grew up in Edmonton, Alberta. Family was working-class; no documented wrestling background in the family, but Benoit was obsessed with wrestling from a young age.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family wrestling background documented; however, growing up in Edmonton with access to Stu Hart's Stampede Wrestling promotion provided direct domain immersion from age 12.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Stu Hart Dungeon training, Stampede Wrestling, Dynamite Kid idol, New Japan dojo, early debut age 18
evidence_summary: Chris Benoit was born in 1967 in Montreal and raised in Edmonton, Alberta. He idolized the Dynamite Kid and Bret Hart from childhood, attending Stampede Wrestling events from age 12. He trained in Stu Hart's famous 'Dungeon' from age 17, debuted for Stampede Wrestling at 18 in November 1985, and won his first championship title at 20 in March 1988. starting_point: Born in 1967 in Montreal, Quebec, Canada to Michael and Margaret Benoit; working-class family, raised in Edmonton, Alberta. No family wrestling background.
current_position: Died on June 24, 2007 at age 40 in Fayetteville, Georgia, USA; final status: WWE and WCW professional wrestler who held 30 championships across multiple promotions.
